cells.title: Carry a capped proof across a rebase when its patch-id matches
cells.action: Per pstack-0-15-port D2. (1) HELPER. `run_git` in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/git.rs sets `.stdin(std::process::Stdio::null())` (search that line), so it cannot feed `git patch-id`. Add beside it one helper, `run_git_stdin(cwd, args, input: &[u8])`, same return shape as `run_git`, that writes `input` to the child's stdin; no `sh -c`, no shell. (2) COMPARE. In packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/phases.rs, `stale_proof_cells` (doc comment starts `/// D4: the capped cells of this feature whose recorded proof predates`) filters `proof.commits` with `run_git(main_root, &["merge-base", "--is-ancestor", &base, commit]).status == Some(1)`. Keep that filter as the first pass. Then, ONLY when its result is non-empty, compute the branch-side patch-ids ONCE: run `git log -p --format=%H <base>..<branch>` with `run_git`, feed its stdout to `git patch-id --stable` with `run_git_stdin`, and read one `<patch-id> <commit>` line per commit. For each commit the first pass flagged, compute its own patch-id the same way (`git show <commit>` fed to `git patch-id --stable`). A flagged commit whose patch-id appears in the branch-side set goes to a NEW list `proof_carried`; the rest stay `proof_stale`. Fail open exactly as the existing code does: any git call that does not exit 0, an empty patch-id, or an empty range leaves the first-pass answer as it was and carries nothing. Thread `proof_carried` beside `proof_stale` through the same struct and the same P3 insert (search `result.insert("proof_stale".into()`), with code `proof_carried`, a `cells` array, and this message: `N capped cell(s) (<ids>) were proven at a commit the rebase rewrote; the patch is unchanged, so the recorded proof still describes this code. Nothing to re-run.` (3) PRINT. packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/handlers.rs renders the human text with `if let Some(stale) = r.get("proof_stale") {` → `  proof-stale: …`; add the sibling `  proof-carried: …` line right after it, same shape. (4) KNOWLEDGE. In docs/knowledge/areas/worktree-parallelism/returning-and-the-merge-gate.md, where it names the `proof-stale` advisory (search `proof-stale`), add one short paragraph naming `proof_carried`, the patch-id rule, and D2 (decision 91835aa0). (5) RED FIRST, required: add one test beside `a_proof_taken_before_the_merge_base_is_named_and_the_merge_still_lands` in packages/bee-rs/crates/bee/src/verbs/worktree/tests.rs that commits work on the branch, caps a cell at that sha, moves main, REBASES the branch onto main (`git rebase main` in the worktree), merges, and asserts: the JSON result carries `proof_carried.cells == ["<id>"]`, no `proof_stale` row names that id, the printed text carries `proof-carried:` and not `proof-stale:` for it, and the merge landed. Run it before the fix and record the red output; then implement and record the green run. Keep the existing stale test green: a plain merge from main still reports `proof_stale`. Record on the cap the wall-clock of the patch-id stream on this repo's longest live branch (one `git log -p` run), the open cost question from CONTEXT.md. cells.action: Two edits, per pstack-0-15-port D1 and D5. EDIT 1 — spoken lines. Line numbers may drift; match on the text. Append to each ` — <reason>` LAST on the line, in the shape the other twenty lines use (see `never build on a red base — the red is the work now: fix it first, then carry on`). `bee orient` prints these lines verbatim, so keep each reason under 12 words; the seven touched lines stay under 140 characters after the edit (a planning bound, nothing enforces it; untouched lines are not yours). EDIT 2 — playbooks. In each of the nine files skills/bee-planning/playbooks/<class>.md, every numbered step states why it holds, in one short clause (`because …`, or an em-dash clause), unless the step already carries one or points at a home that carries it (bugfix step 2 points at worker-details.md and stays as is). Nothing lands in packages/bee/AGENTS.block.md or AGENTS.md. cells.action: Three doctrine edits, per pstack-0-15-port D3, D6 and D4; each rule has ONE home. EDIT 1 — the narrowed re-verify (D3).
